name: Eastern Muya
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Ikeda, Takumi (2002), 'On Pitch Accent in the Mu-Nya Language', LTBA 25.1; also Bai, Junwei (2019), A Grammar of Munya, PhD thesis, James Cook University (JCU repository 403-blocked)

sources.citation: Punzi, Valentina. 2025. Fresh Twigs, Drying Blood, and Popped Corn: The Ephemeral Materiality of Eastern Minyag Ritual Objects. Religions 16(5): 539. doi:10.3390/rel16050539.
sources.note: Ethnography, no linguistics. p.3: Eastern Minyag = Qiangic-speaking community of about seven thousand people east of Gangkar (Gongga) Mountain in Shimian County; language 'not mutually intelligible with the one spoken by the Western Minyag community'; n.2 refers to Punzi 2021 for linguistic differences.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2020. Change Request 2020-043 (submitted by Agnes Conrad & Wang Baobao, 31 Aug 2020): split of mvm Muya/Minyag into Eastern Minyag [emq] and Western Minyag [wmg]; adopted 15 Jan 2021. 6 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone. Identity/bibliography only: Eastern and Western Minyag mutually unintelligible ('enough divergence in the lexicon and phonology'); 'there is exceedingly little published research on Eastern Minyag'; requesters know only three published works treating it: Sun Hongkai 2016 (a word list), Yin Weibin 2012/2013 and 2017 (spatial relations).

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2020. Request for New Language Code Element in ISO 639-3: Eastern Minyag [emq] (Conrad & Wang, associated with CR 2020-043). 4 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Gives names (Eastern Minyag; autonym Munya; Shimian Minyag/Munya/Muya), location (Shimian County, Jiulong County), ~2,000 speakers, oral corpus pending at ELAR; no linguistic description.

sources.citation: Bai, Junwei. 2019. A grammar of Munya. PhD thesis, James Cook University. xxx+546 pp. doi:10.25903/2SHV-X307.
sources.note: Describes WESTERN Muya (west2417; Jiangde village, Pengbuxi, northern sub-dialect): word prosody sec. 2.4 = binary /H/ vs /L/ word-tone (pitch-accent-like) system; the word 'stress' never occurs. On the eastern dialect (this languoid) it has no data: sec. 1.1 'The situation in the eastern dialect area is more obscure, as there is virtually no report on the linguistic situation'; sec. 1.8 'I cannot provide any first-hand information on the eastern Munya area because I did not do any fieldwork there'; sec. 1.9 'Yin (2013, 2017)... are still the only two studies pertaining to the eastern dialect…

sources.citation: Ikeda, Takumi. 2002. On pitch accent in the Mu-nya language. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 25.2: 27-45.
sources.note: Pitch-accent analysis (marked /H/ vs unmarked, no spreading) of the WESTERN dialect (Sade/Shade district, Kangding). Explicitly excludes this languoid, p.27: 'All these descriptions are of the western dialect of Mu-nya, spoken around the Sade district. We have no linguistic information on the eastern dialect spoken in the Shimian district, which might be in danger of extinction.' The earlier world scan named this paper (as LTBA 25.1) for east2351; it does not describe Eastern Muya.

sources.citation: Yang, Zhenfa. 2025. The Mirativity of Existential Verb in Shimian Munya. SSRN preprint 5816628 (posted 27 Nov 2025), doi:10.2139/ssrn.5816628 — and any underlying Chinese dissertation by the same author on 石棉木雅语 (Shimian Muya) grammar.
